title: Coins for Bombs: The Predictive Ability of On-Chain Transfers for Terrorist Attacks
sources_checked: Author package input work/Figures/Figure 3 Data.xlsx (SHA-256 bc459a3aee5eee1a4342ee75592b41ae6f1f4585f2d5a7193a422368672fdead), first sheet fields Date, Out, In, Total; 127 unique daily rows dated 2019-02-25 through 2019-07-01. This is the exact workbook in the accepted predecessor local_inputs.json; no newer workbook vintage was located.

Accepted author code Figures/plotXRPtransfers.R and Codes/READ ME.txt in the named package inventory; the XRP mentions in Codes are only in the README, with no XRP/Ripple/XRPL input builder or preparation script. The code applies the authored 2019 long and short plot windows.

Repository local resource metadata output/feasibility_reproduction/resources/catalog.json, generated 2026-10-27; 959 indexed datasets and 6 resources, with no XRP/Ripple/XRPL match. The catalog warns that this is metadata, not verified access or historical coverage.

Accepted predecessor output/executions/packages/jar-71d04669efdd/report.json and local_inputs.json: the exact workbook hash was staged; predecessor R import reported Date=POSIXct/POSIXt, numeric Out/In/Total, 127 rows and coverage through 2019-07-01; it reported no reference-figure comparison.
changes: Mapped xrp_transfer_plots to the separate author Figure 3 historical Ripple transfers plot at the Gateway Ripple Wallet (GRW), not the main Bitcoin abnormal-volume fit. The main sample ID is included only for the Sri Lanka Easter bombing event context: the paper identifies that bombing in the notable-attack sample (p.15), while Figure 3 plots daily XRP transfers at GRW (p.31). The plot population remains daily XRP date observations.

Expanded the long plot upper cutoff from 2019-07-01 to 2024-07-01 and the short plot cutoffs from 2019-06-01/2019-05-31 to 2024-06-01/2024-05-31, preserving each lower date bound, the author daily aggregation, series, colors and plot settings.

Staged the exact author workbook into work/Figures with the accepted SHA-256. Added computed per-window inclusion markers and an aggregate-only CSV; the only figure outputs are freshly regenerated PDFs.
limitations: The author-supplied workbook supports dates only through 2019-07-01, short of both five-year requested endpoints in 2024. The pooled long window adds only 1 daily grouped date and the short window adds 32 daily workbook rows, all ending 2019-07-01; both are partial extensions.

The supplied package inventory contains no XRP preparation/collection route beyond the plotting script. The 2026-10-27 local catalog snapshot has no XRP/Ripple/XRPL record and explicitly cautions that catalog metadata does not verify access or coverage. No newer compatible local input or route was established, and no source acquisition was performed.

This branch produces descriptive figures, not an estimated coefficient or event-study model. The predecessor notes that no exact reference PDF or visual tolerance was available, so there is no scalar focal estimate or formal figure comparison.

analyses.reason: The accepted standalone XRP plotting branch pools the original daily GRW XRP window (2019-03-29 through 2019-06-30) with the available later dates under a five-year requested endpoint of 2024-06-30. The paper places the Sri Lanka Easter bombing in the notable-attack sample and identifies Figure 3 as daily GRW Ripple transfers; sample_id main is therefore only the event context, not the Bitcoin estimation population.
